title: Machine-Checked Exact-Rational Primal-Dual Cut-Covering and Better-Than-3 Approximation Certificates for 2-Edge-Connected Spanning Subgraphs
abstract: Danciu and Ibrahimpur (arXiv:2611.32924, November 25, 2026) broke the longstanding primal-dual 3-approximation barrier for the minimum-cost 2-edge-connected spanning subgraph (2ECSS) problem, achieving ratio sqrt(3) + 1 ~ 2.73205 in a single phase relative to the natural cut-LP relaxation by growing dual variables of leaves and isolated vertices at rate 1 and nontrivial connected components at rate beta = (sqrt(3)-1)/2. We present a machine-checked, zero-floating-point formalization, exact-Q primal-dual solver, and certificate auditing framework for this algorithm. First, we build an 18-theorem zero-dependency Lean 4 kernel (PrimalDual2ECSS.lean, Lean 4.35.0; 0 sorry, 0 warnings, 0 Classical.choice, 5 zero-axiom theorems) certifying Lemma 3.1 potential descent |V_H| + kappa(H) : 2n -> 2 (T <= 2n - 2), |L| >= 2|C|, Theorem 1.2 cleared incidence expansion, the full cleared Lemma 3.4 disconnected-forest ratio inequality over Z, the quadratic optimality identities (2*beta+1)^2 = 3 and (alpha-1)^2 = 3, strict better-than-3 dominance for every interior rational beta in (0, 1/2), exact continued-fraction convergents (alpha = 11/4, 153/56, 571/209), inductive cut-LP weak duality, and inductive iteration telescoping. Second, we implement a zero-float rational primal-dual 2ECSS engine and the PRIMAL-DUAL-2ECSS-CERT-1.0 verifier spanning four modes. Across 16 canonical certificates, zero-float replay takes 0.036-0.424 ms, matches brute-force 2^11-subset exact OPT = 18 on prism6_weighted, and rejects 57/57 live adversarial forgeries.
